item.title: Treasury Yields Hit Highest Level Since 2002
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Kestra Investment Management Chief Investment Officer Kara Murphy, Vanguard Senior Fixed Income Client Portfolio Manager Joyce Huang, BofA Securities Senior Equity Research Analyst Wamsi Mohan, CH Robinson President & CEO Dave Bozeman, Former Boston Fed President Eric Rosengren, Pivotal Advisors CEO & CIO Tiffany McGhee, UBS Chief Investment Office Fixed Income Strategy Head Leslie Falconio, CHANGE Global Founder & Managing Director Thea Jamison, Coresight Research Founder & CEO Deborah Weinswig, & Babylist CEO Jennifer Hyman. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fmr. Boston Fed Pres: Waiting To Raise Rates Seems Right
item.description: Former Boston Fed President Eric Rosengren described the U.S. economy as middling: inflation has eased more than policymakers expected at their September meeting, while the latest jobs report was somewhat weak. He said the Fed is likely to wait until its final meeting of the year before deciding whether another 25-basis-point hike is needed, rather than act just before the midterm elections. He speaks with Scarlet Fu & Hema Parmar on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Elecciones Brasil: Lula replantea su campaña ante Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Read the story in English
item.dc:creator: Simone Iglesias, Martha Beck and Andrew Rosati

item.title: Brazil’s Right-Wing Shift Highlights a Bigger Trend
item.description: Brazil’s turn to the right matches the ideological switch across Latin America, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Juan Pablo Spinetto says. A Bolsonaro triumph in the runoff would mark the seventh consecutive win by a right-wing presidential candidate in the region in the past year, proof that beyond the problems facing incumbents, a deeper philosophical shift is afoot. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Yemen Says It’s Retaken Mocha as Battle for Bab El-Mandeb Looms
item.description: Yemen’s armed forces wrested control of the Red Sea city of Mocha on Monday after battles with the Iran-backed Houthis, according to state-run Saba, which puts the internationally recognized government closer to taking over the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
item.dc:creator: Sherif Tarek

item.title: Trump’s Nebraska Visit Shows Republican Risks Across the Heartland
item.description: The Senate map keeps shifting.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove

item.title: White House Blocks Politico From Air Force One Trip
item.description: The White House is refusing to allow Politico to travel Monday on Air Force One with President Donald Trump, the latest salvo in a fight that has seen officials restrict access to certain media outlets.
item.dc:creator: Skylar Woodhouse and Hannah Miller

item.title: Stocks Get Tech Lift Despite Renewed Bond Losses
item.description: A rally in giant technology companies drove stocks higher, overshadowing concerns about still-elevated oil prices and bond yields. The S&P 500 approached a record as a gauge of megacaps climbed 1.3%. Political upheaval in Europe and fiscal worries sent the euro to its weakest since May 2025, boosting the dollar’s haven appeal. We get reaction from Michael Ball, Bloomberg News Macro Strategist. Realty Income CEO Sumit Roy joins for a look at the state of the real estate market. Astrea London founder Nathalie Morrison & actress Sarah Jessica Parker, Astrea's Global Creative Director discuss their jewelry venture. Bloomberg Supreme Court reporter Greg Stohr previews the high court's upcoming term. All on the latest episode of "Bloomberg Businessweek Daily. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says Terror Threats Forced B-1 Bombers Out of UK Base
item.description: President Donald Trump said fresh threats of terror attacks prompted the US to move its B-1 bombers from their base in the UK, contradicting his top diplomat who had earlier described the move as part of a regular rotation.
item.dc:creator: Courtney McBride and Ellen Milligan

item.title: Brazil Election 2026: Bolsonaro’s Lead Has Lula Looking for Campaign Reset
item.description: To Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Sunday’s second-place finish to Flávio Bolsonaro stung all the more because he’d believed he could secure a knockout over his right-wing challenger.
item.dc:creator: Simone Iglesias, Martha Beck and Andrew Rosati

item.title: Obama Plans Detroit Rally With El-Sayed in Tight Senate Race
item.description: Former President Barack Obama and President Donald Trump both plan to campaign in Michigan during the coming weeks in a showdown to bolster their candidates, especially in the key Senate race between Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and opponent Mike Rogers, just ahead of the Nov. 3 election.
item.dc:creator: David Welch

item.title: Trump Plans Tax-Exempt Diesel Relief
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the Midterm elections. On today's show, former Acting White House Chief of Staff Mick Mulvaney, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Gulf Oil Chief Energ Advisor Tom Kloza. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Probably Not Enough Money to Fix Paxton Campaign, Says Mulvaney
item.description: Mick Mulvaney, former acting chief of staff in the first Trump administration, said Ken Paxton, the Republican contender for the US Senate seat in Texas, is the 'weakest candidate' in this election and that there's 'probably not enough money to fix' him. Mulvaney also weighed in on Paxton's comments to lobbyists blaming the White House for his issues campaigning. Mulvaney said that if Paxton wins it will be due to Donald Trump and that the president is the only person who can get Ken Paxton over the finish line in November. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: EE.UU. arresta a presunta espía china por vigilar al hijo del presidente de Taiwán
item.description: Una mujer sospechosa de espiar para China al vigilar al hijo del presidente de Taiwán y a su familia fue detenida por las autoridades estadounidenses antes de abordar un vuelo a Shanghái, según el FBI, en momentos en que persisten las tensiones entre EE.UU. y China.
item.dc:creator: Josh Xiao and Myles Miller

item.title: ‘Porky’ Nears Lima Comeback Despite Peru’s Ban on Reelection
item.description: A Peruvian party led by a combative conservative holds a narrow lead in Lima’s mayoral race. There’s just one problem: the law bans immediate reelection for mayors, leaving voters unsure whether he can take the job.
item.dc:creator: Carla Samon Ros

item.title: Bolsonaro refuerza su influencia en el Congreso de Brasil
item.description: La apuesta de Jair Bolsonaro por construir una dinastía política da frutos: su familia amplía su poder en el legislativo y apunta ahora a reforzar su posición frente al Tribunal Supremo.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Rosati

item.title: Trump Could Ease Restrictions on a Variety of Diesel
item.description: The Trump administration is expected to lift restrictions on using so-called red dyed diesel. The fuel is usually used in farm equipment. Details are still forthcoming. Bloomberg's Tyler Kendall reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Spain’s Sánchez Calls for Snap Election After Housing Plan Fails
item.description:
Spain’s Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called a snap election after parliament rejected his plan to intervene in the housing market, amid demonstrations across Spain.
It’s the latest in a series of crises for his minority government, as Daniel Basteiro explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Plans to Ease Limits on Tax-Exempt Diesel Variety
item.description: President Donald Trump is preparing to ease limits restricting the use of a tax-exempt variety of diesel, his latest bid to pare costs for the essential fuel ahead of the November midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy

item.title: FBI Says China Agent Spied on Taiwan President’s Son in US
item.description: A woman suspected of spying for China by surveilling the Taiwanese president’s son and his family has been arrested by the US before she could board a flight to Shanghai, according to the Federal Bureau of Investigation, as tensions linger between the rival superpowers.
item.dc:creator: Josh Xiao and Myles Miller
